eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Pakistan Meteorological Department and global models such as ECMWF and GFS indicate peak temperatures in Karachi on May 24 will likely settle between 34°C and 36°C, aligning with the closely matched market-implied odds around these outcomes. Karachi’s coastal position on the Arabian Sea drives sea-breeze moderation that typically caps afternoon highs despite strong solar heating under clear pre-monsoon skies and a stable high-pressure ridge. Low-level humidity and light to moderate westerly winds further influence the exact peak by enhancing evaporative cooling or limiting boundary-layer mixing. Historical May climatology shows average highs near 35–36°C, with urban heat-island effects occasionally adding 1–2°C in the city center. New model runs and official updates over the next 48 hours will refine these variables and determine whether the high reaches the upper or lower end of the current consensus range.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from PAGASA and global models point to Manila’s May 24 maximum temperature peaking near 36°C, driven by strong solar insolation under pre-monsoon easterly flow, light boundary-layer winds, and the urban heat-island effect that routinely adds 1–2°C to daytime readings at Ninoy Aquino International Airport. Afternoon convective cloud cover and isolated thunderstorms remain the key variables that could cap the high at 35°C or allow brief clearing to push readings to 37°C, producing the tight 37.5–27.5 percent split between those two outcomes. Historical late-May climatology shows typical maxima of 33–34°C, so current conditions represent modestly above-average heating; the low probabilities assigned to 38°C or higher reflect limited potential for stronger warming before the onset of more frequent monsoon moisture.
